initiative: DECA BMOR: The Game Table — Stakeholder Analysis

stakeholders.name: DECA Judges
stakeholders.notes: They want to see rigorous research, logical strategy, and professional presentation. They'll penalize weak data, unrealistic numbers, or superficial analysis. High influence, medium alignment — they're not on our side until we prove ourselves.

stakeholders.name: Team Members (3 people)
stakeholders.notes: All aligned and motivated. But they're high school students — judges will scrutinize depth of analysis accordingly.

stakeholders.name: Frisco ISD Administration
stakeholders.notes: Likely supportive but won't fight for this. Need them to sign off on competition entry.

stakeholders.name: Board Game Cafe Owners (competitors)
stakeholders.role: Industry professionals who could be interviewed
stakeholders.notes: Unlikely to respond to a high school student's interview request. This is a research gap.

stakeholders.name: Frisco Community / Parents
stakeholders.notes: Frisco is a family-oriented community. Parents control household spending. If they don't see value, the business fails.

stakeholders.name: UT Dallas Students
stakeholders.notes: Strong potential fit — board games, affordable entertainment, proximity. But they're busy and have many options.

stakeholders.name: Nerdvana (Competitor)
stakeholders.notes: They are our biggest competitive threat. If they extend hours to daytime, our main differentiator disappears. They're an engaged skeptic — paying attention, not convinced we pose a real threat.
